title: Robust facility location (2-ASP(Q) with weak constraints)
description: Open facilities at the least total cost so that every customer is still served by a nearby open facility when any one open facility fails: an exists-forall problem with an objective on the outer level, as in 2-ASP(Q) programs with weak constraints. The abstraction opens facilities cheapest first (a #minimize, A.solve(optimal)); the check picks a failure and a customer left without service. The refinement says: open another facility near that customer. The first opening that no failure refutes is optimal.

fragments.name: shared
abstraction
fragments.text:
% The outer level: which sites to open, at the least total cost (a weak constraint).
{ open(S) : site(S,_) }.
:~ open(S), site(S,C). [C,S]
#show open/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): open sites, cheapest first.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the open sites.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The inner level: at most one open facility fails, and some customer has no other open
% site near (with no failure: a customer without any open site near).
{ fail(S) : open(S) } 1.
1 { lost(U) : customer(U) } 1.
:- lost(U), near(U,S), open(S), not fail(S).
#show fail/1.
#show lost/1.

% The customer stays lost while every site near it other than the failed one stays closed:
% one of them must open.
relevant(open(S)) :- lost(U), near(U,S), not fail(S).
fragments.description: Looks for a failure that leaves a customer without service (solver C).

fragments.name: check_short
fragments.text:
% The inner level: at most one open facility fails, and some customer has no other open
% site near (with no failure: a customer without any open site near).
{ fail(S) : open(S) } 1.
1 { lost(U) : customer(U) } 1.
:- lost(U), near(U,S), open(S), not fail(S).
#show fail/1.
#show lost/1.

% The customer stays lost while every site near it other than the failed one stays closed:
% one of them must open.
relevant(open(S)) :- lost(U), near(U,S), not fail(S).
% Variant shortest: prefer a failure whose clause has the fewest sites.
#minimize { 1,S : relevant(open(S)) }.
fragments.description: The check with a #minimize over the relevant sites, for the variant shortest.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# 2-ASP(Q) with a weak constraint on the outer level: the cheapest opening first; the first
# one that no failure refutes is optimal (chapter 11). The refinement is a clause, so every
# opening it removes leaves the same customer stranded by the same failure. G.clause(X)
# takes the values from the counterexample: for a customer whose only near site failed (or
# with no near site) it is the empty clause; then A has no candidate left and the loop
# ends exhausted, with no solution.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M:
        log "no robust opening"
        break
    track lower = M.cost
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(X))
    else:
        accept M
        stop

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Baseline: every refuted opening is blocked on its own.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M:
        log "no robust opening"
        break
    track lower = M.cost
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.block(M))
    else:
        accept M
        stop

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The counterexample with the fewest relevant sites (optimal): the shortest clause.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M:
        log "no robust opening"
        break
    track lower = M.cost
    X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(X))
    else:
        accept M
        stop

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to four counterexamples per opening, one clause each.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M:
        log "no robust opening"
        break
    track lower = M.cost
    Xs = C.models(assume G(M), limit 4)
    if Xs.size > 0:
        for X in Xs:
            A.add(G.clause(X))
    else:
        accept M
        stop

generators.name: sites
generators.description: n sites with opening cost 2..8; u customers, each near k random sites.
generators.text:
% sites: n sites with a random opening cost (2..8); u customers, each near a random k-subset of the sites
site(S,@int(2, 8, cost, S)) :- S = 1..n.
near(U,S) :- U = 1..u, S = 1..n, @subset(k, n, S, U) = 1.
#show site/2.  #show near/2.

spaces.name: maps
spaces.text:
% every map: sites 1..size with opening cost 1..2, customers 1..size near some sites
sid(1..size).  uid(1..size).
1 { site(S,C) : C = 1..2 } 1 :- sid(S).
{ near(U,S) : uid(U), sid(S) }.
